```{r setup, include=FALSE}

  echo = TRUE,
  warning = FALSE,
  message = FALSE,
  fig.width = 10,
  fig.height = 7,
  dpi = 300
)

# Load libraries
library(tidyverse)
library(ggplot2)
library(ggrepel)
library(pheatmap)
library(RColorBrewer)
library(patchwork)
library(DT)
library(readxl)

# Set paths
project_dir <- "A:/Dropbox/LOY_paralogs/projects/crispr_screen/ht1080_loy_screen_2"
results_dir <- file.path(project_dir, "results/drugZ_analysis")
dir.create(results_dir, showWarnings = FALSE, recursive = TRUE)

# Data paths - drugZ results instead of MAGeCK
count_file <- file.path(project_dir, "count/ht1080_screen2_R1.count.txt")
count_summary_file <- file.path(project_dir, "count/ht1080_screen2_R1.countsummary.txt")
drugz_file <- file.path(project_dir, "results/drugZ/LOY_vs_CTRL_unfiltered.txt")
mageck_file <- file.path(project_dir, "test/POST_LOY_vs_CTRL.gene_summary.txt")  # For LFC values
sgrna_summary_file <- file.path(project_dir, "test/POST_LOY_vs_CTRL.sgrna_summary.txt")
rnaseq_de_file <- "A:/Dropbox/LOY_paralogs/data/RNAseq/AUG_13_2025_LOY_A549_HT1080/DE/ht1080_LOY_v_WT_DE_noY.csv"

# Analysis parameters
FDR_THRESHOLD <- 0.25
ZSCORE_THRESHOLD <- 2  # Using normZ for effect size threshold

# Custom theme
theme_crispr <- function() {
  theme_bw() +
    theme(
      panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
      text = element_text(size = 12),
      plot.title = element_text(size = 14, face = "bold"),
      legend.position = "bottom"
    )
}

# Color palettes
colors_condition <- c("LOY" = "#E41A1C", "CTRL" = "#377EB8")
colors_timepoint <- c("D0" = "#984EA3", "POST" = "#4DAF4A")
colors_significance <- c("Depleted" = "#2166AC", "Enriched" = "#B2182B", "NS" = "grey70")
```

# Project Overview

This analysis examines a CRISPR screen comparing **Y- (LOY)** vs **Y+ (CTRL)** HT1080 cells using **drugZ** algorithm results to identify genetic vulnerabilities specific to cells that have lost the Y chromosome.

**Key parameters:**

-   **Library**: Brunello (77,441 sgRNAs targeting 19,114 genes)
-   **Comparison**: POST_LOY vs POST_CTRL
-   **Analysis method**: drugZ (sumZ statistic)
-   **FDR threshold**: `r FDR_THRESHOLD`
-   **Note**: D0 samples have low mapping rates (\~21%) and are excluded from main analysis

------------------------------------------------------------------------

# Module 1: Quality Control {.tabset}

## 1.1 Load Data

```{r load-data}
# Load count matrix
counts <- read_tsv(count_file, show_col_types = FALSE)
colnames(counts)[1:2] <- c("sgRNA", "Gene")

# Load count summary (MAGeCK QC metrics)
count_summary <- read_tsv(count_summary_file, show_col_types = FALSE)

# Display count summary
count_summary %>%
  dplyr::mutate(
    Percentage = scales::percent(Percentage, accuracy = 0.1),
    Mapped = scales::comma(Mapped),
    Reads = scales::comma(Reads)
  ) %>%
  dplyr::select(Label, Reads, Mapped, Percentage, Zerocounts, GiniIndex) %>%
  dplyr::rename(
    Sample = Label,
    `Total Reads` = Reads,
    `Mapped Reads` = Mapped,
    `Mapping Rate` = Percentage,
    `Zero Counts` = Zerocounts,
    `Gini Index` = GiniIndex
  ) %>%
  knitr::kable(caption = "MAGeCK Count Summary") %>%
  kableExtra::kable_styling(bootstrap_options = c("striped", "hover"))
```

```{r sample-metadata}
# Create sample metadata
sample_info <- tibble(
  Sample = c("D0_CTRL", "D0_LOY", "POST_CTRL_REP1", "POST_CTRL_REP2", "POST_LOY_REP1", "POST_LOY_REP2"),
  Condition = c("CTRL", "LOY", "CTRL", "CTRL", "LOY", "LOY"),
  Timepoint = c("D0", "D0", "POST", "POST", "POST", "POST"),
  Replicate = c("pooled", "pooled", "1", "2", "1", "2")
) %>%
  dplyr::left_join(count_summary %>% dplyr::select(Label, Mapped, Percentage, GiniIndex),
            by = c("Sample" = "Label"))

sample_info %>%
  knitr::kable(caption = "Sample Metadata") %>%
  kableExtra::kable_styling(bootstrap_options = c("striped", "hover"))
```

## 1.2 Library Size & Mapping

```{r library-size-plot, fig.height=5}
# Library size bar chart
p_libsize <- count_summary %>%
  mutate(
    Sample = Label,
    Condition = ifelse(grepl("LOY", Label), "LOY", "CTRL"),
    Timepoint = ifelse(grepl("D0", Label), "D0", "POST"),
    Mapped_M = Mapped / 1e6
  ) %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = reorder(Sample, -Mapped_M), y = Mapped_M, fill = Condition)) +
  geom_col(color = "black", linewidth = 0.3) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = colors_condition) +
  labs(
    title = "Mapped Reads per Sample",
    x = "Sample",
    y = "Mapped Reads (millions)"
  ) +
  theme_crispr() +
  theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1))

# Mapping rate bar chart
p_maprate <- count_summary %>%
  mutate(
    Sample = Label,
    Condition = ifelse(grepl("LOY", Label), "LOY", "CTRL"),
    Timepoint = ifelse(grepl("D0", Label), "D0", "POST"),
    MapPct = Percentage * 100
  ) %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = reorder(Sample, -MapPct), y = MapPct, fill = Timepoint)) +
  geom_col(color = "black", linewidth = 0.3) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 50, linetype = "dashed", color = "red") +
  scale_fill_manual(values = colors_timepoint) +
  labs(
    title = "Mapping Rate per Sample",
    subtitle = "Red line = 50% threshold; D0 samples have low mapping (~21%)",
    x = "Sample",
    y = "Mapping Rate (%)"
  ) +
  theme_crispr() +
  theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1))

p_libsize + p_maprate
```

**Key observation**: D0 samples have \~21% mapping rate compared to \~85% for POST samples. This suggests a library preparation or technical issue with D0 samples. **D0 samples should be excluded from primary differential analysis.**

## 1.3 Gini Index

The Gini index measures library uniformity (0 = perfectly uniform, 1 = all reads in one sgRNA).

```{r gini-plot, fig.height=4}
count_summary %>%
  mutate(
    Sample = Label,
    Condition = ifelse(grepl("LOY", Label), "LOY", "CTRL"),
    Timepoint = ifelse(grepl("D0", Label), "D0", "POST")
  ) %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = reorder(Sample, GiniIndex), y = GiniIndex, fill = Condition)) +
  geom_col(color = "black", linewidth = 0.3) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0.2, linetype = "dashed", color = "red") +
  scale_fill_manual(values = colors_condition) +
  labs(
    title = "Gini Index per Sample",
    subtitle = "Red line = 0.2 threshold; lower is better",
    x = "Sample",
    y = "Gini Index"
  ) +
  coord_flip() +
  theme_crispr()
```

All samples have Gini indices below 0.12, indicating good library uniformity.

## 1.5 Sample Correlation

```{r correlation-heatmap, fig.height=6, fig.width=7}
# Calculate correlation matrix (Spearman)
count_matrix <- counts %>%
  dplyr::select(-sgRNA, -Gene) %>%
  as.matrix()

cor_matrix <- cor(count_matrix, method = "spearman")

# Create annotation
annotation_col <- data.frame(
  Condition = ifelse(grepl("LOY", colnames(cor_matrix)), "LOY", "CTRL"),
  Timepoint = ifelse(grepl("D0", colnames(cor_matrix)), "D0", "POST"),
  row.names = colnames(cor_matrix)
)

annotation_colors <- list(
  Condition = colors_condition,
  Timepoint = colors_timepoint
)

pheatmap(
  cor_matrix,
  display_numbers = TRUE,
  number_format = "%.3f",
  color = colorRampPalette(c("#2166AC", "white", "#B2182B"))(100),
  breaks = seq(0.8, 1, length.out = 101),
  annotation_col = annotation_col,
  annotation_colors = annotation_colors,
  main = "Sample Correlation (Spearman)",
  fontsize = 10
)
```

## 1.5b Replicate Correlation Scatter Plots

```{r replicate-correlation, fig.height=5, fig.width=10}
# Compute log2 CPM (also used downstream in PCA chunk)
lib_sizes <- colSums(count_matrix)
cpm_matrix <- t(t(count_matrix) / lib_sizes * 1e6)
log2_cpm <- log2(cpm_matrix + 1)

# Create data frame with log2 CPM for scatter plots
log2_cpm_df <- as.data.frame(log2_cpm) %>%
  rownames_to_column("sgRNA")

# CTRL replicates correlation
cor_ctrl <- cor(log2_cpm_df$POST_CTRL_REP1, log2_cpm_df$POST_CTRL_REP2, method = "pearson")

p_ctrl_rep <- ggplot(log2_cpm_df, aes(x = POST_CTRL_REP1, y = POST_CTRL_REP2)) +
  geom_point(size = 0.5, alpha = 0.3, color = colors_condition["CTRL"]) +
  geom_abline(slope = 1, intercept = 0, linetype = "dashed", color = "red") +
  annotate("text", x = 2, y = max(log2_cpm_df$POST_CTRL_REP2) - 1,
           label = paste0("R = ", round(cor_ctrl, 3)),
           size = 5, fontface = "bold") +
  labs(
    title = "CTRL Biological Replicates",
    x = "POST_CTRL_REP1 (log2 CPM)",
    y = "POST_CTRL_REP2 (log2 CPM)"
  ) +
  theme_crispr() +
  coord_fixed()

# LOY replicates correlation
cor_loy <- cor(log2_cpm_df$POST_LOY_REP1, log2_cpm_df$POST_LOY_REP2, method = "pearson")

p_loy_rep <- ggplot(log2_cpm_df, aes(x = POST_LOY_REP1, y = POST_LOY_REP2)) +
  geom_point(size = 0.5, alpha = 0.3, color = colors_condition["LOY"]) +
  geom_abline(slope = 1, intercept = 0, linetype = "dashed", color = "red") +
  annotate("text", x = 2, y = max(log2_cpm_df$POST_LOY_REP2) - 1,
           label = paste0("R = ", round(cor_loy, 3)),
           size = 5, fontface = "bold") +
  labs(
    title = "LOY Biological Replicates",
    x = "POST_LOY_REP1 (log2 CPM)",
    y = "POST_LOY_REP2 (log2 CPM)"
  ) +
  theme_crispr() +
  coord_fixed()

# Combine plots
p_ctrl_rep + p_loy_rep

cat("\nReplicate Correlations (Pearson R):\n")
cat("  CTRL (REP1 vs REP2):", round(cor_ctrl, 4), "\n")
cat("  LOY (REP1 vs REP2):", round(cor_loy, 4), "\n")
```

## 1.6 PCA

```{r pca-plot, fig.height=5, fig.width=5}
# PCA on CPM-normalized counts (accounts for library size differences)
# Calculate CPM (counts per million)
lib_sizes <- colSums(count_matrix)
cpm_matrix <- t(t(count_matrix) / lib_sizes * 1e6)

# Log2 transform CPM values
log2_cpm <- log2(cpm_matrix + 1)

# Remove zero-variance rows (constant across samples) before PCA
row_vars <- apply(log2_cpm, 1, var)
log2_cpm_filtered <- log2_cpm[row_vars > 0, ]
cat("Using CPM-normalized counts for PCA\n")
cat("Removed", sum(row_vars == 0), "zero-variance sgRNAs for PCA\n")

pca_result <- prcomp(t(log2_cpm_filtered), scale. = TRUE)

# Extract variance explained
var_explained <- summary(pca_result)$importance[2, 1:2] * 100

# PCA plot
pca_df <- as.data.frame(pca_result$x[, 1:2]) %>%
  rownames_to_column("Sample") %>%
  mutate(
    Condition = ifelse(grepl("LOY", Sample), "LOY", "CTRL"),
    Timepoint = ifelse(grepl("D0", Sample), "D0", "POST")
  )

ggplot(pca_df, aes(x = PC1, y = PC2, color = Condition, shape = Timepoint)) +
  geom_point(size = 5) +
  geom_text_repel(aes(label = Sample), size = 3) +
  scale_color_manual(values = colors_condition) +
  labs(
    title = "PCA of sgRNA Counts (CPM-normalized)",
    x = paste0("PC1 (", round(var_explained[1], 1), "% variance)"),
    y = paste0("PC2 (", round(var_explained[2], 1), "% variance)")
  ) +
  theme_crispr()
```

## 1.7 Non-Targeting Control Analysis

```{r control-guide-analysis, fig.height=5}
# Load sgRNA summary to get LFC values
sgrna_summary <- read_tsv(sgrna_summary_file, show_col_types = FALSE)

# Extract non-targeting controls
ntc_guides <- sgrna_summary %>%
  filter(Gene == "Non-Targeting-Control")

cat("Number of Non-Targeting Control sgRNAs:", nrow(ntc_guides), "\n")

# Calculate summary statistics for NTC LFCs
ntc_stats <- ntc_guides %>%
  summarise(
    n = n(),
    mean_lfc = mean(LFC),
    sd_lfc = sd(LFC),
    median_lfc = median(LFC),
    q025 = quantile(LFC, 0.025),
    q975 = quantile(LFC, 0.975)
  )

cat("\nNon-Targeting Control LFC Statistics:\n")
cat("  Mean LFC:", round(ntc_stats$mean_lfc, 3), "\n")
cat("  SD LFC:", round(ntc_stats$sd_lfc, 3), "\n")
cat("  95% CI:", round(ntc_stats$q025, 3), "to", round(ntc_stats$q975, 3), "\n")

# Plot NTC distribution
p_ntc <- ggplot(ntc_guides, aes(x = LFC)) +
  geom_histogram(aes(y = after_stat(density)), bins = 50, fill = "grey70", color = "grey40") +
  geom_density(color = "black", linewidth = 1) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 0, linetype = "dashed", color = "red") +
  geom_vline(xintercept = c(ntc_stats$q025, ntc_stats$q975),
             linetype = "dotted", color = "blue") +
  labs(
    title = "Non-Targeting Control sgRNA LFC Distribution",
    subtitle = paste0("n = ", ntc_stats$n, " guides | Mean = ", round(ntc_stats$mean_lfc, 3),
                      " | SD = ", round(ntc_stats$sd_lfc, 3)),
    x = "Log2 Fold Change (POST_LOY vs POST_CTRL)",
    y = "Density"
  ) +
  theme_crispr()

p_ntc

# Save NTC stats for later use
ntc_lfc_values <- ntc_guides$LFC
```

The non-targeting control distribution provides our null expectation. sgRNAs outside the 95% CI (blue dotted lines) are more likely to represent true biological effects.

## 1.8 QC Summary

```{r qc-summary}
# Create QC summary table
qc_summary <- count_summary %>%
  mutate(
    Sample = Label,
    Condition = ifelse(grepl("LOY", Label), "LOY", "CTRL"),
    Timepoint = ifelse(grepl("D0", Label), "D0", "POST"),
    QC_Status = case_when(
      Percentage < 0.5 ~ "FAIL - Low mapping",
      GiniIndex > 0.2 ~ "WARNING - High Gini",
      TRUE ~ "PASS"
    )
  ) %>%
  dplyr::select(Sample, Condition, Timepoint, Percentage, GiniIndex, Zerocounts, QC_Status)

qc_summary %>%
  mutate(Percentage = scales::percent(Percentage, accuracy = 0.1)) %>%
  knitr::kable(caption = "QC Summary") %>%
  kableExtra::kable_styling(bootstrap_options = c("striped", "hover")) %>%
  kableExtra::row_spec(which(qc_summary$QC_Status != "PASS"), background = "#FFCCCC")
```

**QC Conclusions:**

1.  **D0 samples FAIL** QC due to low mapping rates (\~21%)
2.  All POST samples **PASS** QC with good mapping (\>84%) and low Gini indices (\<0.09)
3.  Non-targeting controls center around LFC = `r round(ntc_stats$mean_lfc, 2)` with SD = `r round(ntc_stats$sd_lfc, 2)`
4.  **Recommendation**: Use only POST samples for differential analysis

# Module 2: CRISPR Screen Visualization (drugZ) {.tabset}

## 2.1 Load drugZ Results

```{r load-drugz}
# Load drugZ gene summary
drugz_results <- read_tsv(drugz_file, show_col_types = FALSE)

# Rename columns to standard format
# drugZ columns: GENE, sumZ, numObs, normZ, pval_synth, rank_synth, fdr_synth, pval_supp, rank_supp, fdr_supp
gene_summary <- drugz_results %>%
  rename(
    id = GENE,
    num = numObs
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    # Add significance categories based on drugZ FDR
    neg_fdr = fdr_synth,  # synthetic lethality = depletion
    pos_fdr = fdr_supp,   # suppressor = enrichment
    neg_lfc = sumZ,       # Use sumZ as effect size (negative = depleted)
    pos_lfc = -sumZ,      # Positive selection would be opposite sign
    neg_significant = neg_fdr < FDR_THRESHOLD,
    pos_significant = pos_fdr < FDR_THRESHOLD,
    category = case_when(
      neg_fdr < FDR_THRESHOLD ~ "Depleted",
      pos_fdr < FDR_THRESHOLD ~ "Enriched",
      TRUE ~ "NS"
    )
  )

# Summary counts
n_depleted <- sum(gene_summary$neg_significant, na.rm = TRUE)
n_enriched <- sum(gene_summary$pos_significant, na.rm = TRUE)

cat("drugZ Results Summary:\n")
cat("Significant genes at FDR <", FDR_THRESHOLD, ":\n")
cat("  Depleted (synthetic lethality):", n_depleted, "\n")
cat("  Enriched (suppressor):", n_enriched, "\n")
cat("  Total genes tested:", nrow(gene_summary), "\n")

# Show drugZ-specific columns
cat("\ndrugZ statistics for top 20 depleted genes:\n")
gene_summary %>%
  arrange(fdr_synth) %>%
  head(20) %>%
  select(id, sumZ, normZ, fdr_synth, rank_synth, num) %>%
  knitr::kable(digits = 4) %>%
  print()
```

## 2.2 Waterfall Plot

```{r waterfall-plot, fig.height=3, fig.width=4}
# Prepare data - rank by normZ (ascending: most negative/depleted first)
waterfall_data <- gene_summary %>%
  arrange(normZ) %>%
  mutate(rank = row_number())

# Number of genes to label on each end
n_depleted_label <- 10
n_enriched_label <- 3

# Get top depleted (lowest normZ) and enriched (highest normZ) genes
top_depleted <- waterfall_data %>% slice_head(n = n_depleted_label)
top_enriched <- waterfall_data %>% slice_tail(n = n_enriched_label)

# Publication-style waterfall plot
p_waterfall <- ggplot(waterfall_data, aes(x = rank, y = normZ)) +
  geom_point(size = 0.5, color = "black") +
  # Label top depleted genes in red (italic)
  geom_text_repel(
    data = top_depleted,
    aes(label = id),
    color = "#B2182B",
    fontface = "italic",
    size = 3,
    nudge_x = 1500,
    direction = "y",
    hjust = 0,
    segment.size = 0.2,
    segment.color = "grey70",
    box.padding = 0.05,
    point.padding = 0.1,
    max.overlaps = 20
  ) +
  # Label top enriched genes in blue (italic)
  geom_text_repel(
    data = top_enriched,
    aes(label = id),
    color = "#2166AC",
    fontface = "italic",
    size = 3,
    nudge_x = -1500,
    direction = "y",
    hjust = 1,
    segment.size = 0.2,
    segment.color = "grey70",
    box.padding = 0.05,
    point.padding = 0.1,
    max.overlaps = 20
  ) +
  labs(
    title = "HT1080 + LOY",
    x = "Gene Rank",
    y = "NormZ score"
  ) +
  theme_classic() +
  theme(
    plot.title = element_text(size = 12, face = "bold"),
    axis.title = element_text(size = 11),
    axis.text = element_text(size = 10),
    plot.margin = margin(5, 15, 5, 5)
  )

p_waterfall

# Save
ggsave(file.path(results_dir, "module2_waterfall.pdf"), p_waterfall,
       width = 6, height = 5)
```

```{r waterfall-saga, fig.height=3, fig.width=4}
# SAGA complex genes
saga_genes <- c("ATXN7", "ATXN7L3", "ENY2", "KAT2A", "KAT2B", "PAAF1",
```

## 2.2b-ii Waterfall Plot - All SAGA Members

Unlike 2.2b (which labels only SAGA members passing the FDR threshold), this
plot highlights **every** SAGA subunit present in the screen, colored by whether
it reaches significance.

```{r waterfall-saga-all, fig.height=3, fig.width=4}
# All SAGA members present in the screen (no FDR filter), colored by significance.
# `saga_genes` is defined above in the 2.2b chunk.
waterfall_saga_all <- waterfall_data %>%
  mutate(
    is_saga = id %in% saga_genes,
    saga_sig = case_when(
      is_saga & fdr_synth < FDR_THRESHOLD ~ paste0("SAGA (FDR < ", FDR_THRESHOLD, ")"),
      is_saga ~ "SAGA (NS)",
      TRUE ~ "Other"
    )
  )

saga_all_in_plot <- waterfall_saga_all %>% filter(is_saga)

cat("SAGA genes in list:", length(saga_genes), "\n")
cat("SAGA members present in screen (all labeled):", nrow(saga_all_in_plot), "\n")

sig_col <- paste0("SAGA (FDR < ", FDR_THRESHOLD, ")")
p_waterfall_saga_all <- ggplot(waterfall_saga_all, aes(x = rank, y = normZ)) +
  geom_point(data = filter(waterfall_saga_all, !is_saga),
             size = 0.5, color = "grey70") +
  geom_point(data = saga_all_in_plot,
             aes(color = saga_sig), size = 2) +
  scale_color_manual(values = setNames(c("#E41A1C", "#377EB8"),
                                       c(sig_col, "SAGA (NS)")),
                     name = NULL) +
  geom_text_repel(
    data = saga_all_in_plot,
    aes(label = id, color = saga_sig),
    fontface = "italic",
    size = 2.5,
    max.overlaps = Inf,
    segment.size = 0.2,
    segment.color = "grey70",
    box.padding = 0.15,
    show.legend = FALSE
  ) +
  labs(
    title = "HT1080 + LOY",
    subtitle = "All SAGA complex members labeled",
    x = "Gene Rank",
    y = "NormZ score"
  ) +
  theme_classic() +
  theme(
    plot.title = element_text(size = 12, face = "bold"),
    plot.subtitle = element_text(size = 9),
    axis.title = element_text(size = 11),
    axis.text = element_text(size = 10),
```

## 2.2b-iii Waterfall Plot - Essential SAGA Members

Highlights only the SAGA subunits reported as **essential / functionally
required** in Batty et al. 2026, *Nat Commun* 17:3410
(doi:10.1038/s41467-026-71613-7), *"Disruption of the SAGA CORE triggers
collateral degradation of KAT2A."*

```{r waterfall-saga-essential, fig.height=3, fig.width=4}
# SAGA subunits observed as essential / functionally required, per
# Batty et al. 2026, Nat Commun 17:3410 (doi:10.1038/s41467-026-71613-7):
#   - TADA1, TAF5L, TAF6L : SAGA CORE subunits necessary for KAT2A stability and
#       complex integrity (central finding; validated by IF, sucrose-gradient
#       fractionation, and dTAG acute degradation)
#   - TAF12               : explicitly "an essential gene" (shared SAGA CORE /
#       TFIID); loss also reduces KAT2A (co-translational handshake with TADA1)
#   - SF3B3, SF3B5        : SPL module, "common essentiality" (rapid sgRNA
#       dropout comparable to the RAD21 / MYC essential controls)
#   - TADA2B, TADA3, SGF29: HAT module; knockout significantly reduced KAT2A
# (The DUB module - USP22, ENY2, ATXN7, ATXN7L3 - was dispensable, and the
#  TRRAP reporter effect was an artifact, so those are excluded.)
saga_essential <- c("TADA1", "TAF5L", "TAF6L", "TAF12",
                    "SF3B3", "SF3B5", "TADA2B", "TADA3", "SGF29")

waterfall_saga_ess <- waterfall_data %>%
  mutate(is_ess = id %in% saga_essential)

saga_ess_in_plot <- waterfall_saga_ess %>% filter(is_ess)

cat("Essential SAGA members present in screen:", nrow(saga_ess_in_plot),
    "of", length(saga_essential), "\n\n")
saga_ess_in_plot %>%
  arrange(normZ) %>%
  select(id, normZ, sumZ, fdr_synth) %>%
  mutate(across(where(is.numeric), ~signif(., 3))) %>%
  print()

p_waterfall_saga_ess <- ggplot(waterfall_saga_ess, aes(x = rank, y = normZ)) +
  geom_point(data = filter(waterfall_saga_ess, !is_ess),
             size = 0.5, color = "grey70") +
  geom_point(data = saga_ess_in_plot,
             size = 2.5, color = "#7B3294") +
  geom_text_repel(
    data = saga_ess_in_plot,
    aes(label = id),
    color = "#7B3294",
    fontface = "italic",
    size = 3,
    nudge_x = 1500,
    direction = "y",
    hjust = 0,
    segment.size = 0.2,
    segment.color = "grey70",
    box.padding = 0.1,
    max.overlaps = Inf
  ) +
  labs(
    title = "HT1080 + LOY",
    subtitle = "Essential SAGA subunits (Batty et al. 2026, Nat Commun)",
    x = "Gene Rank",
    y = "NormZ score"
  ) +
  theme_classic() +
```

## 2.2d Waterfall Plot - X-Y Paralogs

Highlights the **X-linked partner** of each known X-Y paralog (gametolog) pair.
When the Y chromosome is lost, the Y-linked paralog is gone, so the X-linked
partner becomes the sole source of that function - the core dosage-compensation
rationale for LOY-specific dependencies.


## 2.3 Volcano Plot - Negative Selection (Synthetic Lethality)

```{r volcano-neg, fig.height=7, fig.width=10}
# Define STAGA complex genes (CORUM:6664) for highlighting
staga_genes <- c("TAF6L", "SUPT20H", "ATXN7L3", "TADA2B", "TADA1")

# Prepare volcano data for negative selection (synthetic lethality)
volcano_neg <- gene_summary %>%
  mutate(
    neg_log10_fdr = -log10(fdr_synth),
    is_staga = id %in% staga_genes,
    label = case_when(
      fdr_synth < 0.01 ~ id,  # Label top hits
      is_staga ~ id,  # Always label STAGA genes
      TRUE ~ NA_character_
    )
  )

# Top 20 depleted genes for labeling
top_depleted <- volcano_neg %>%
  filter(neg_significant) %>%
  arrange(fdr_synth) %>%
  head(20) %>%
  pull(id)

volcano_neg <- volcano_neg %>%
  mutate(label = ifelse(id %in% top_depleted, id, label))

# Volcano plot with STAGA highlighting
p_volcano_neg <- ggplot(volcano_neg, aes(x = sumZ, y = neg_log10_fdr)) +
  # Non-significant points
  geom_point(data = filter(volcano_neg, !neg_significant & !is_staga),
             color = "grey70", alpha = 0.5, size = 1) +
  # Significant points (not STAGA)
  geom_point(data = filter(volcano_neg, neg_significant & !is_staga),
             color = colors_significance["Depleted"], alpha = 0.7, size = 2) +
  # STAGA complex genes (highlighted with purple triangles, smaller with black outline)
  geom_point(data = filter(volcano_neg, is_staga),
             aes(shape = neg_significant),
             fill = "#8E44AD", color = "black", size = 2.5, stroke = 0.5) +
  scale_shape_manual(values = c("TRUE" = 24, "FALSE" = 2),  # 24 = filled triangle, 2 = open triangle
                     labels = c("TRUE" = "Significant", "FALSE" = "Not significant"),
                     name = "STAGA Status") +
  # Labels for non-STAGA genes
  geom_text_repel(
    data = filter(volcano_neg, !is_staga & !is.na(label)),
    aes(label = label),
    size = 3,
    max.overlaps = 30,
    segment.size = 0.2,
    fontface = "italic"
  ) +
  # Labels for STAGA genes (purple, larger)
  geom_text_repel(
    data = filter(volcano_neg, is_staga),
    aes(label = id),
    color = "#8E44AD",
    size = 4,
    max.overlaps = 30,
    segment.size = 0.2,
    fontface = "bold.italic"
  ) +
  # Threshold lines
  geom_hline(yintercept = -log10(FDR_THRESHOLD), linetype = "dashed", color = "red") +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 0, linetype = "solid", color = "grey50") +
  labs(
    title = "Volcano Plot: Synthetic Lethality (drugZ)",
    subtitle = paste0("FDR < ", FDR_THRESHOLD, " threshold (red line) | ",
                      "Purple = STAGA complex genes (CORUM:6664)"),
    x = "drugZ sumZ Score (negative = depleted)",
    y = "-log10(FDR)"
  ) +
  theme_crispr() +
  coord_cartesian(xlim = c(-25, 15))

p_volcano_neg

# Save
ggsave(file.path(results_dir, "module2_volcano_neg.pdf"), p_volcano_neg,
       width = 10, height = 7)
```

## 2.4b Volcano Plot - Log2FC with SAGA Highlight

```{r volcano-lfc, fig.height=5, fig.width=6}
# Load MAGeCK results for LFC values
mageck_results <- read_tsv(mageck_file, show_col_types = FALSE)

  ) %>%
  mutate(

saga_volcano <- volcano_lfc_data %>% filter(is_saga)

# Proper volcano plot: Log2FC vs -log10(p-value)
```

## 2.6 X-Linked Gene Analysis

```{r x-linked-analysis, fig.height=8}
# Define expanded X-linked gene list (15 genes including RPS4X, EIF1AX, ZFX)
x_linked_genes <- c("DDX3X", "TIMM8A", "USP9X", "KDM6A", "KDM5C", "ATRX",
                    "SMC1A", "HDAC6", "BCOR", "BCORL1", "HUWE1", "UBA1",
                    "RPS4X", "EIF1AX", "ZFX")

# Focus on X-linked genes
x_linked_data <- gene_summary %>%
  filter(id %in% x_linked_genes) %>%
  arrange(fdr_synth) %>%
  select(id, num, fdr_synth, sumZ, normZ, fdr_supp)

cat("X-Linked Genes in Screen (drugZ results):\n\n")

x_linked_data %>%
  mutate(
    fdr_synth = signif(fdr_synth, 3),
    fdr_supp = signif(fdr_supp, 3),
    sumZ = round(sumZ, 3),
    normZ = round(normZ, 3)
  ) %>%
  knitr::kable(caption = "X-linked genes - potential LOY vulnerabilities") %>%
  kableExtra::kable_styling(bootstrap_options = c("striped", "hover"))

# Bar plot of X-linked gene sumZ scores
p_xlinked <- x_linked_data %>%
  mutate(
    significant = fdr_synth < FDR_THRESHOLD,
    id = fct_reorder(id, sumZ)
  ) %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = id, y = sumZ, fill = significant)) +
  geom_col(color = "black", linewidth = 0.3) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0, color = "black") +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c("TRUE" = "#FF6600", "FALSE" = "grey70"),
                    labels = c("TRUE" = "Significant", "FALSE" = "NS")) +
  coord_flip() +
  labs(
    title = "X-Linked Gene Depletion in LOY Cells (drugZ)",
    subtitle = paste0("FDR < ", FDR_THRESHOLD),
    x = "Gene",
    y = "drugZ sumZ Score (negative = depleted)",
    fill = "Status"
  ) +
  theme_crispr()

p_xlinked
```

**Key X-linked findings:**

-   **DDX3X** is the top hit overall (FDR = `r signif(x_linked_data$fdr_synth[1], 3)`, sumZ = `r round(x_linked_data$sumZ[1], 2)`), suggesting strong synthetic lethality with LOY
-   **BCORL1** and other X-linked genes also show significant depletion
-   These genes may escape X-inactivation and provide dosage-sensitive vulnerabilities

## 2.7 Per-Gene sgRNA Plots

Generate individual plots for each significant gene showing its sgRNAs against the non-targeting control distribution.

```{r sgrna-plot-function}
# Function to create per-gene sgRNA plot
create_sgrna_plot <- function(gene_name, sgrna_data, ntc_data, gene_stats) {

  # Get sgRNAs for this gene
  gene_sgrnas <- sgrna_data %>%
    filter(Gene == gene_name)

  # Get gene-level stats from drugZ
  stats <- gene_stats %>%
    filter(id == gene_name)

  if(nrow(gene_sgrnas) == 0) return(NULL)

  # Create plot
  p <- ggplot() +
    # NTC distribution (background)
    geom_density(data = ntc_data, aes(x = LFC),
                 fill = "grey80", color = "grey50", alpha = 0.7) +
    # Gene sgRNAs as vertical lines
    geom_vline(data = gene_sgrnas, aes(xintercept = LFC),
               color = "#2166AC", linewidth = 1, alpha = 0.8) +
    # Gene sgRNAs as points at top
    geom_point(data = gene_sgrnas,
               aes(x = LFC, y = 0.05),
               color = "#2166AC", size = 3, shape = 17) +
    # Zero line
    geom_vline(xintercept = 0, linetype = "dashed", color = "red", alpha = 0.5) +
    # Labels
    labs(
      title = gene_name,
      subtitle = paste0("drugZ FDR = ", signif(stats$fdr_synth, 3),
                        " | sumZ = ", round(stats$sumZ, 2),
                        " | ", stats$num, " sgRNAs"),
      x = "Log2 Fold Change",
      y = "Density"
    ) +
    theme_crispr() +
    theme(
      plot.title = element_text(size = 12, face = "bold"),
      plot.subtitle = element_text(size = 9),
      axis.line.x.bottom = element_line(color = "black", linewidth = 0.5),
      panel.border = element_rect(color = "black", fill = NA, linewidth = 0.5)
    ) +
    coord_cartesian(xlim = c(-6, 4))

  return(p)
}
```

### Depleted Genes sgRNA Plots

```{r sgrna-plots-depleted, fig.height=4, fig.width=6, results='asis'}

cat("Generating sgRNA plots for", length(sig_depleted), "depleted genes...\n\n")

depleted_plots <- list()
for(i in 1:n_plots) {
  gene <- sig_depleted[i]
  p <- create_sgrna_plot(gene, sgrna_summary, ntc_guides, gene_summary)
  if(!is.null(p)) {

}

      width = 8, height = 5)
  for(p in depleted_plots) {

  }

}
```

# Module 3: RNA-seq Integration {.tabset}

## 3.1 Load RNA-seq Data

```{r load-rnaseq}
# Load RNA-seq differential expression data
rnaseq_de <- read_csv(rnaseq_de_file, show_col_types = FALSE)

cat("RNA-seq DE data loaded:\n")
cat("  Genes:", nrow(rnaseq_de), "\n")
cat("  Columns:", paste(colnames(rnaseq_de), collapse = ", "), "\n")

# Preview
head(rnaseq_de) %>%
  mutate(across(where(is.numeric), ~signif(., 3))) %>%
  knitr::kable(caption = "RNA-seq DE data preview") %>%
  kableExtra::kable_styling(bootstrap_options = c("striped", "hover"))
```

## 3.2 Merge CRISPR and RNA-seq Data

```{r merge-data}
# Merge by gene name
# drugZ uses 'id' (renamed from GENE), RNA-seq uses 'gene_name'
integrated_data <- gene_summary %>%
  inner_join(
    rnaseq_de %>% select(gene_name, logFC, logCPM, PValue, FDR),
    by = c("id" = "gene_name")
  ) %>%
  rename(
    rnaseq_logFC = logFC,
    rnaseq_logCPM = logCPM,
    rnaseq_pvalue = PValue,
    rnaseq_fdr = FDR
  )

cat("Data integration summary:\n")
cat("  drugZ genes:", nrow(gene_summary), "\n")
cat("  RNA-seq genes:", nrow(rnaseq_de), "\n")
cat("  Merged genes:", nrow(integrated_data), "\n")
cat("  Match rate:", scales::percent(nrow(integrated_data) / nrow(gene_summary)), "\n")
```

## 3.3 Add Chromosome Annotation

```{r add-chromosome}
# Try to add chromosome info using biomaRt or a predefined list
# For now, use a curated list of X-linked genes

# Expanded X-linked gene list (known escapees and LOY-relevant)
x_chromosome_genes <- c(
  # Known X-inactivation escapees
  "DDX3X", "KDM6A", "KDM5C", "USP9X", "EIF1AX", "ZFX", "PRKX",
  "RPS4X", "TXLNG", "SMC1A", "HDAC6", "TIMM8A", "ATRX",

)

  mutate(

cat("\nX-linked genes in integrated dataset:", n_x_linked, "\n")
```

## 3.4 Concordance Analysis

```{r concordance-analysis}
# Define significance thresholds
CRISPR_FDR <- FDR_THRESHOLD
RNASEQ_FDR <- 0.05

# Classify genes by concordance
integrated_data <- integrated_data %>%
  mutate(
    # Significance flags
    crispr_sig_neg = fdr_synth < CRISPR_FDR,
    crispr_sig_pos = fdr_supp < CRISPR_FDR,
    rnaseq_sig = rnaseq_fdr < RNASEQ_FDR,

    # Direction of effect
    crispr_direction = case_when(
      crispr_sig_neg ~ "Depleted",
      crispr_sig_pos ~ "Enriched",
      TRUE ~ "NS"
    ),
    rnaseq_direction = case_when(
      rnaseq_sig & rnaseq_logFC < 0 ~ "Down",
      rnaseq_sig & rnaseq_logFC > 0 ~ "Up",
      TRUE ~ "NS"
    ),

    # Concordance category
    concordance = case_when(
      # Concordant: CRISPR depleted + RNA-seq down (gene important, low expression in LOY)
      crispr_sig_neg & rnaseq_sig & rnaseq_logFC < 0 ~ "Concordant (Depleted/Down)",
      # Concordant: CRISPR enriched + RNA-seq up
      crispr_sig_pos & rnaseq_sig & rnaseq_logFC > 0 ~ "Concordant (Enriched/Up)",
      # Discordant patterns
      crispr_sig_neg & rnaseq_sig & rnaseq_logFC > 0 ~ "Discordant (Depleted/Up)",
      crispr_sig_pos & rnaseq_sig & rnaseq_logFC < 0 ~ "Discordant (Enriched/Down)",
      # One significant only
      crispr_sig_neg & !rnaseq_sig ~ "CRISPR only (Depleted)",
      crispr_sig_pos & !rnaseq_sig ~ "CRISPR only (Enriched)",
      !crispr_sig_neg & !crispr_sig_pos & rnaseq_sig ~ "RNA-seq only",
      TRUE ~ "Neither significant"
    )
  )

# Summary table
concordance_summary <- integrated_data %>%
  count(concordance) %>%
  arrange(desc(n)) %>%
  mutate(percent = scales::percent(n / sum(n)))

cat("Concordance Summary:\n\n")
concordance_summary %>%
  knitr::kable(caption = "Gene classification by CRISPR and RNA-seq significance") %>%
  kableExtra::kable_styling(bootstrap_options = c("striped", "hover"))

# Save concordance summary
write_csv(concordance_summary, file.path(results_dir, "module3_concordance_summary.csv"))
```

## 3.5 CRISPR vs RNA-seq Scatter Plot

```{r integration-scatter, fig.height=8, fig.width=10}
# Calculate correlation (using sumZ as CRISPR effect size)
cor_pearson <- cor(integrated_data$sumZ, integrated_data$rnaseq_logFC,
                   use = "complete.obs", method = "pearson")
cor_spearman <- cor(integrated_data$sumZ, integrated_data$rnaseq_logFC,
                    use = "complete.obs", method = "spearman")

cat("Correlation between drugZ sumZ and RNA-seq logFC:\n")
cat("  Pearson r =", round(cor_pearson, 3), "\n")
cat("  Spearman rho =", round(cor_spearman, 3), "\n")

# Prepare labels for key genes
integrated_data <- integrated_data %>%
  mutate(
    label = case_when(
      # Always label X-linked significant hits
      is_x_linked & crispr_sig_neg ~ id,
      # Label concordant hits
      concordance %in% c("Concordant (Depleted/Down)", "Concordant (Enriched/Up)") ~ id,
      # Label top CRISPR hits
      fdr_synth < 0.05 ~ id,
      TRUE ~ NA_character_
    )
  )

# Define colors for concordance
concordance_colors <- c(
  "Concordant (Depleted/Down)" = "#2166AC",
  "Concordant (Enriched/Up)" = "#B2182B",
  "Discordant (Depleted/Up)" = "#762A83",
  "Discordant (Enriched/Down)" = "#1B7837",
  "CRISPR only (Depleted)" = "#67A9CF",
  "CRISPR only (Enriched)" = "#EF8A62",
  "RNA-seq only" = "#F7F7F7",
  "Neither significant" = "grey80"
)

# Scatter plot (using sumZ for x-axis)
p_scatter <- ggplot(integrated_data,
                    aes(x = sumZ, y = rnaseq_logFC, color = concordance)) +
  # Background points (neither significant)
  geom_point(data = filter(integrated_data, concordance == "Neither significant"),
             alpha = 0.3, size = 1) +
  # Significant points
  geom_point(data = filter(integrated_data, concordance != "Neither significant"),
             alpha = 0.7, size = 2) +
  # X-linked genes as triangles
  geom_point(data = filter(integrated_data, is_x_linked & crispr_sig_neg),
             aes(x = sumZ, y = rnaseq_logFC),
             color = "#FF6600", size = 4, shape = 17) +
  # Labels
  geom_text_repel(
    aes(label = label),
    size = 2.5,
    max.overlaps = 30,
    segment.size = 0.2,
    fontface = "italic"
  ) +
  # Reference lines
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0, linetype = "dashed", color = "grey50") +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 0, linetype = "dashed", color = "grey50") +
  # Trend line
  geom_smooth(method = "lm", color = "black", linetype = "solid",
              se = TRUE, alpha = 0.2, linewidth = 0.5) +
  # Colors
  scale_color_manual(values = concordance_colors, name = "Category") +
  # Labels
  labs(
    title = "drugZ CRISPR Screen vs RNA-seq Integration",
    subtitle = paste0("Pearson r = ", round(cor_pearson, 3),
                      " | Spearman rho = ", round(cor_spearman, 3),
                      " | Orange triangles = X-linked"),
    x = "drugZ sumZ Score (negative = depleted)",
    y = "RNA-seq Log2 Fold Change (LOY vs WT)"
  ) +
  theme_crispr() +
  theme(legend.position = "right") +
  coord_cartesian(xlim = c(-25, 15), ylim = c(-5, 5))

p_scatter

# Save
ggsave(file.path(results_dir, "module3_crispr_vs_rnaseq.pdf"), p_scatter,
       width = 10, height = 8)
```

```{r x-linked-integration, fig.height=6, fig.width=10}
    select(id, sumZ, rnaseq_logFC, fdr_synth) %>%
    pivot_longer(cols = c(sumZ, rnaseq_logFC),

    mutate(

    geom_hline(yintercept = 0, color = "black") +
    scale_fill_manual(values = c("CRISPR (sumZ)" = "#2166AC", "RNA-seq (logFC)" = "#B2182B")) +
    coord_flip() +
    labs(
      title = "X-Linked Genes: CRISPR (drugZ) vs RNA-seq",
      subtitle = "Comparison of effect sizes between assays",
      x = "Gene",
      y = "Effect Size (sumZ or logFC)",
      fill = "Assay"
    ) +
    theme_crispr()

  print(p_xlinked_compare)

  ggsave(file.path(results_dir, "module3_x_linked_comparison.pdf"), p_xlinked_compare,
         width = 10, height = 6)
}
```

## 3.7 Quadrant Analysis

```{r quadrant-analysis, fig.height=6}
# Count genes in each quadrant (based on direction of sumZ and rnaseq_logFC)
quadrant_counts <- integrated_data %>%
  mutate(
    quadrant = case_when(
      sumZ < 0 & rnaseq_logFC < 0 ~ "CRISPR- / RNA-",
      sumZ < 0 & rnaseq_logFC > 0 ~ "CRISPR- / RNA+",
      sumZ > 0 & rnaseq_logFC < 0 ~ "CRISPR+ / RNA-",
      sumZ > 0 & rnaseq_logFC > 0 ~ "CRISPR+ / RNA+",
      TRUE ~ "On axis"
    )
  ) %>%
  count(quadrant) %>%
  mutate(percent = scales::percent(n / sum(n)))

cat("Quadrant Analysis:\n\n")
quadrant_counts %>%
  knitr::kable(caption = "Gene distribution by CRISPR and RNA-seq direction") %>%
  kableExtra::kable_styling(bootstrap_options = c("striped", "hover"))

# Quadrant interpretation
cat("\nInterpretation:\n")
cat("- CRISPR- / RNA-: Genes depleted in screen AND downregulated in LOY\n")
cat("  (May be essential genes with reduced expression in LOY)\n\n")
cat("- CRISPR- / RNA+: Genes depleted in screen BUT upregulated in LOY\n")
cat("  (Interesting: compensatory upregulation of essential genes?)\n\n")
cat("- CRISPR+ / RNA-: Genes enriched in screen AND downregulated in LOY\n")
cat("  (Tumor suppressors? Loss provides growth advantage)\n\n")
cat("- CRISPR+ / RNA+: Genes enriched in screen AND upregulated in LOY\n")
cat("  (Oncogenes? Both elevated and drive growth)\n")

# Bar plot of quadrant distribution
p_quadrant <- quadrant_counts %>%
  filter(quadrant != "On axis") %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = reorder(quadrant, -n), y = n, fill = quadrant)) +
  geom_col(color = "black", linewidth = 0.3) +
  geom_text(aes(label = paste0(n, "\n(", percent, ")")),
            vjust = -0.3, size = 3) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c("CRISPR- / RNA-" = "#2166AC",
                                "CRISPR- / RNA+" = "#762A83",
                                "CRISPR+ / RNA-" = "#1B7837",
                                "CRISPR+ / RNA+" = "#B2182B")) +
  labs(
    title = "Quadrant Analysis: CRISPR vs RNA-seq Direction",
    subtitle = "Distribution of genes by effect direction",
    x = "Quadrant",
    y = "Number of Genes"
  ) +
  theme_crispr() +
  theme(legend.position = "none",
        axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 0, hjust = 0.5)) +
  ylim(0, max(quadrant_counts$n) * 1.15)

p_quadrant
```

# Module 4: Pathway Analysis {.tabset}

## 4.1 Setup and Gene Ranking

```{r pathway-setup}
# Load pathway analysis packages
library(fgsea)
library(msigdbr)

# Create ranked gene list for GSEA
# Strategy: Use normZ directly (negative = depleted, already normalized)
# This ranks strongly depleted genes at the top (most negative)

ranked_genes <- gene_summary %>%
  filter(!is.na(normZ)) %>%
  arrange(normZ) %>%
  distinct(id, .keep_all = TRUE)

# Create named vector for fgsea (using normZ as the ranking statistic)
gene_ranks <- setNames(ranked_genes$normZ, ranked_genes$id)

cat("Gene ranking summary (using drugZ normZ):\n")
cat("  Total ranked genes:", length(gene_ranks), "\n")
cat("  Range:", round(min(gene_ranks), 2), "to", round(max(gene_ranks), 2), "\n")
cat("  Median:", round(median(gene_ranks), 2), "\n")

# Show top depleted and enriched
cat("\nTop 10 most depleted (most negative normZ):\n")
head(sort(gene_ranks), 10)

cat("\nTop 10 most enriched (most positive normZ):\n")
tail(sort(gene_ranks), 10)
```

## 4.2 MSigDB Hallmark Pathways

```{r gsea-hallmark, fig.height=8, fig.width=10}
# Get MSigDB Hallmark gene sets
hallmark_sets <- msigdbr(species = "Homo sapiens", category = "H") %>%
  select(gs_name, gene_symbol) %>%
  group_by(gs_name) %>%
  summarise(genes = list(gene_symbol), .groups = "drop")

# Convert to list format for fgsea
hallmark_pathways <- setNames(hallmark_sets$genes, hallmark_sets$gs_name)

cat("Loaded", length(hallmark_pathways), "Hallmark pathways\n")

# Run fgsea
set.seed(42)
gsea_hallmark <- fgsea(
  pathways = hallmark_pathways,
  stats = gene_ranks,
  minSize = 15,
  maxSize = 500,
  nPermSimple = 10000
)

# Sort by NES and filter significant
gsea_hallmark <- gsea_hallmark %>%
  as_tibble() %>%
  arrange(pval) %>%
  mutate(
    direction = ifelse(NES > 0, "Enriched in LOY", "Depleted in LOY"),
    pathway_short = gsub("HALLMARK_", "", pathway)
  )

# Display results
cat("\nSignificant Hallmark pathways (padj < 0.25):\n\n")

gsea_hallmark %>%
  filter(padj < 0.25) %>%
  select(pathway_short, NES, pval, padj, size) %>%
  mutate(
    NES = round(NES, 3),
    pval = signif(pval, 3),
    padj = signif(padj, 3)
  ) %>%
  knitr::kable(caption = "Significant Hallmark pathways") %>%
  kableExtra::kable_styling(bootstrap_options = c("striped", "hover"))

# Bar plot of top pathways
n_show <- min(20, nrow(gsea_hallmark))
p_hallmark_bar <- gsea_hallmark %>%
  head(n_show) %>%
  mutate(pathway_short = fct_reorder(pathway_short, NES)) %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = pathway_short, y = NES, fill = direction)) +
  geom_col(color = "black", linewidth = 0.3) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0, color = "black") +
  coord_flip() +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c("Depleted in LOY" = "#2166AC",
                                "Enriched in LOY" = "#B2182B")) +
  labs(
    title = "GSEA: MSigDB Hallmark Pathways (drugZ ranking)",
    subtitle = "Ranked by drugZ normZ score",
    x = "Pathway",
    y = "Normalized Enrichment Score (NES)",
    fill = "Direction"
  ) +
  theme_crispr() +
  theme(axis.text.y = element_text(size = 9))

p_hallmark_bar

ggsave(file.path(results_dir, "module4_gsea_hallmark_bar.pdf"), p_hallmark_bar,
       width = 10, height = 8)

# Save results
write_csv(gsea_hallmark, file.path(results_dir, "module4_gsea_hallmark.csv"))
```

## 4.3 KEGG Pathways

```{r gsea-kegg, fig.height=8, fig.width=10}
# Get KEGG gene sets
kegg_sets <- msigdbr(species = "Homo sapiens",
                     category = "C2",
                     subcategory = "CP:KEGG_LEGACY") %>%
  select(gs_name, gene_symbol) %>%
  group_by(gs_name) %>%
  summarise(genes = list(gene_symbol), .groups = "drop")

kegg_pathways <- setNames(kegg_sets$genes, kegg_sets$gs_name)

cat("Loaded", length(kegg_pathways), "KEGG pathways\n")

# Run fgsea
set.seed(42)
gsea_kegg <- fgsea(
  pathways = kegg_pathways,
  stats = gene_ranks,
  minSize = 15,
  maxSize = 500,
  nPermSimple = 10000
)

gsea_kegg <- gsea_kegg %>%
  as_tibble() %>%
  arrange(pval) %>%
  mutate(
    direction = ifelse(NES > 0, "Enriched in LOY", "Depleted in LOY"),
    pathway_short = gsub("KEGG_", "", pathway)
  )

# Display significant results
cat("\nSignificant KEGG pathways (padj < 0.25):\n\n")

gsea_kegg %>%
  filter(padj < 0.25) %>%
  select(pathway_short, NES, pval, padj, size) %>%
  mutate(
    NES = round(NES, 3),
    pval = signif(pval, 3),
    padj = signif(padj, 3)
  ) %>%
  head(30) %>%
  knitr::kable(caption = "Significant KEGG pathways") %>%
  kableExtra::kable_styling(bootstrap_options = c("striped", "hover"))

# Bar plot
n_show_kegg <- min(25, nrow(gsea_kegg))
p_kegg_bar <- gsea_kegg %>%
  head(n_show_kegg) %>%
  mutate(pathway_short = fct_reorder(pathway_short, NES)) %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = pathway_short, y = NES, fill = direction)) +
  geom_col(color = "black", linewidth = 0.3) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0, color = "black") +
  coord_flip() +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c("Depleted in LOY" = "#2166AC",
                                "Enriched in LOY" = "#B2182B")) +
  labs(
    title = "GSEA: KEGG Pathways (drugZ ranking)",
    subtitle = "Ranked by drugZ normZ score",
    x = "Pathway",
    y = "Normalized Enrichment Score (NES)",
    fill = "Direction"
  ) +
  theme_crispr() +
  theme(axis.text.y = element_text(size = 8))

p_kegg_bar

ggsave(file.path(results_dir, "module4_gsea_kegg_bar.pdf"), p_kegg_bar,
       width = 10, height = 8)

write_csv(gsea_kegg, file.path(results_dir, "module4_gsea_kegg.csv"))
```

## 4.4 SAGA Complex Analysis

The SAGA (Spt-Ada-Gcn5 Acetyltransferase) complex is a key chromatin-modifying complex involved in transcriptional regulation. Multiple SAGA subunits appear in our top hits.

```{r saga-analysis, fig.height=6, fig.width=10}
# Define SAGA complex genes
saga_genes <- c("ATXN7", "ATXN7L3", "ENY2", "KAT2A", "KAT2B", "PAAF1",
                "SF3B3", "SF3B5", "SGF29", "SUPT20H", "SUPT20HL1", "SUPT20HL2",
                "SUPT3H", "SUPT7L", "TADA1", "TADA2A", "TADA2B", "TADA3",
                "TAF10", "TAF12", "TAF5", "TAF5L", "TAF6", "TAF6L",
                "TAF9", "TRRAP", "USP22")

# Extract SAGA genes from drugZ screen results
saga_in_screen <- gene_summary %>%
  filter(id %in% saga_genes) %>%
  arrange(fdr_synth) %>%
  select(id, fdr_synth, sumZ, normZ, num)

cat("SAGA Complex Subunits in Screen (drugZ):\n")
cat("  Total SAGA genes:", length(saga_genes), "\n")
cat("  Found in screen:", nrow(saga_in_screen), "\n")
cat("  Significant (FDR <", FDR_THRESHOLD, "):",
    sum(saga_in_screen$fdr_synth < FDR_THRESHOLD, na.rm = TRUE), "\n\n")

# Display table
saga_in_screen %>%
  mutate(
    significant = ifelse(fdr_synth < FDR_THRESHOLD, "***", ""),
    fdr_synth = signif(fdr_synth, 3),
    sumZ = round(sumZ, 3),
    normZ = round(normZ, 3)
  ) %>%
  knitr::kable(caption = "SAGA complex subunits in drugZ CRISPR screen") %>%
  kableExtra::kable_styling(bootstrap_options = c("striped", "hover"))

# Visualize SAGA complex depletion
p_saga <- saga_in_screen %>%
  mutate(
    significant = fdr_synth < FDR_THRESHOLD,
    id = fct_reorder(id, sumZ)
  ) %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = id, y = sumZ, fill = significant)) +
  geom_col(color = "black", linewidth = 0.3) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0, color = "black") +
  scale_fill_manual(
    values = c("TRUE" = "#8E44AD", "FALSE" = "grey70"),
    labels = c("TRUE" = paste0("FDR < ", FDR_THRESHOLD), "FALSE" = "NS")
  ) +
  coord_flip() +
  labs(
    title = "SAGA Complex Subunit Depletion in LOY Cells (drugZ)",
    subtitle = paste0("Multiple subunits show significant depletion (FDR < ", FDR_THRESHOLD, ")"),
    x = "SAGA Subunit",
    y = "drugZ sumZ Score (negative = depleted)",
    fill = "Significance"
  ) +
  theme_crispr() +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom")

print(p_saga)

ggsave(file.path(results_dir, "module4_saga_complex.pdf"), p_saga,
       width = 10, height = 6)
```

```{r save-module5}
  ),

    gene_summary %>% arrange(fdr_synth) %>% slice(1) %>% pull(id),
    as.character(signif(gene_summary %>% arrange(fdr_synth) %>% slice(1) %>% pull(fdr_synth), 4)),
    as.character(round(gene_summary %>% arrange(fdr_synth) %>% slice(1) %>% pull(sumZ), 2)),
    as.character(sum(integrated_data$is_x_linked & integrated_data$crispr_sig_neg, na.rm = TRUE)),
    as.character(round(cor_pearson, 3)),
    as.character(sum(integrated_data$concordance == "Concordant (Depleted/Down)", na.rm = TRUE))
  )
)
```

# Module 10: Summary Excel Export {.tabset}

This module creates a comprehensive Excel workbook for collaborators with all drugZ screen results, expression data, and annotations.

## 10.1 Build Gene Summary Table

```{r module10-gene-summary}
library(openxlsx)

cat("===== BUILDING GENE SUMMARY TABLE (drugZ) =====\n\n")

# Start with drugZ gene summary
gene_summary_export <- gene_summary %>%
  select(
    Gene = id,
    n_sgRNAs = num,
    drugZ_sumZ = sumZ,
    drugZ_normZ = normZ,
    drugZ_fdr_synth = fdr_synth,
    drugZ_rank_synth = rank_synth,
    drugZ_fdr_supp = fdr_supp,
    drugZ_rank_supp = rank_supp
  )

# Add chromosome info
gene_summary_export <- gene_summary_export %>%
  mutate(
    chromosome = ifelse(Gene %in% x_chromosome_genes, "X", "Autosome"),
    is_x_linked = chromosome == "X"
  )

# Add RNA-seq data if available
if(exists("rnaseq_de")) {
  rnaseq_slim <- rnaseq_de %>%
    select(gene_name, logFC, logCPM, FDR) %>%
    rename(
      Gene = gene_name,
      RNAseq_logFC = logFC,
      RNAseq_logCPM = logCPM,
      RNAseq_FDR = FDR
    )

  gene_summary_export <- gene_summary_export %>%
    left_join(rnaseq_slim, by = "Gene")
}

# Add CRISPR direction classification
gene_summary_export <- gene_summary_export %>%
  mutate(
    CRISPR_direction = case_when(
      drugZ_fdr_synth < 0.25 & drugZ_sumZ < 0 ~ "Depleted",
      drugZ_fdr_supp < 0.25 & drugZ_sumZ > 0 ~ "Enriched",
      TRUE ~ "NS"
    )
  )

# Reorder columns
gene_summary_export <- gene_summary_export %>%
  select(
    Gene, chromosome, is_x_linked,
    n_sgRNAs,
    drugZ_sumZ, drugZ_normZ, drugZ_fdr_synth, drugZ_rank_synth,
    drugZ_fdr_supp, drugZ_rank_supp,
    CRISPR_direction,
    everything()
  ) %>%
  arrange(drugZ_fdr_synth)

cat(sprintf("Gene summary table: %d genes x %d columns\n", nrow(gene_summary_export), ncol(gene_summary_export)))
```

## 10.2 Export to Excel

```{r module10-export-excel}
cat("===== EXPORTING TO EXCEL =====\n\n")

# Create workbook
wb <- createWorkbook()

# Add Gene Summary sheet
addWorksheet(wb, "Gene_Summary_drugZ")
writeData(wb, "Gene_Summary_drugZ", gene_summary_export)

# Format header
header_style <- createStyle(
  textDecoration = "bold",
  fgFill = "#4472C4",
  fontColour = "white",
  halign = "center"
)
addStyle(wb, "Gene_Summary_drugZ", header_style, rows = 1, cols = 1:ncol(gene_summary_export), gridExpand = TRUE)

# Auto-width columns
setColWidths(wb, "Gene_Summary_drugZ", cols = 1:ncol(gene_summary_export), widths = "auto")

# Save workbook
excel_output <- file.path(results_dir, "ht1080_loy_screen_drugZ_summary.xlsx")
saveWorkbook(wb, excel_output, overwrite = TRUE)

cat(sprintf("Excel file saved: %s\n", excel_output))
cat(sprintf("  - Tab 1 (Gene_Summary_drugZ): %d rows x %d columns\n", nrow(gene_summary_export), ncol(gene_summary_export)))
```
